summary:
Allwork.Space reports that Belgium's flexible office market has passed 1 million square meters for the first time, citing data from Coworking Europe. The sector now accounts for 4.3% of total Belgian office stock, spanning 591 locations and 1,035,935 square meters, with both floor space and location count growing roughly 8% year over year.

Revenue growth is lagging physical expansion. Market turnover reached 387 million euros in 2025, up from about 50 million euros in 2015, but turnover growth slowed to roughly 5% in 2026, trailing the 8% growth in floor space and locations. The gap is attributed to price competition driving revenue per square meter down. Sector EBITDA averages about 20% of turnover, yet operating profit sits below 3%, partly because opening new centers carries high costs.

The market remains fragmented. IWG, which operates the Regus and Spaces brands, is the largest player in Belgium with 56 locations and more than 121,000 square meters. Local operators Officenter and Silversquare follow with 14 and 11 locations respectively. More than half of all sites are independently operated.

Penetration varies sharply by city: around 12% in Geel and more than 11% in Hasselt, versus approximately 4% in Brussels, indicating stronger relative flex adoption in smaller regional cities than in the capital.

The piece is a market-sizing update rather than a workplace operations or technology story. It does not address visitor management, desk or room booking tooling, hybrid policy design, or workplace analytics software, though it is relevant context for flexible workspace supply and coworking operator economics.
